definitions.explanation: The meat of a chicken used as food.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{鶏肉|とりにく}を{食|た}べたい。
examples.english: I want to eat chicken today.

examples.japanese: {鶏肉|とりにく}と{野菜|やさい}を{炒|いた}める。
スーパーで{安|やす}い{鶏肉|とりにく}を{見|み}つけたから、{今日|きょう}は{唐揚|からあ}げにしよう。
examples.english: I found cheap chicken at the supermarket, so let's make fried chicken today.

examples.japanese: うちの{子供|こども}は{鶏肉|とりにく}が{大好|だいす}きで、{毎週|まいしゅう}{食|た}べたがる。
examples.english: Our child loves chicken and wants to eat it every week.

notes:
{鶏肉|とりにく} specifically refers to chicken as a food ingredient. The kanji {鶏|にわとり} means the live bird, while {鶏肉|とりにく} is the meat used in cooking.

ALTERNATE TERMS:
- チキン: used for Western-style dishes (チキンカツ, チキンナゲット)
- {鳥肉|とりにく}: alternate kanji using {鳥|とり} (bird) instead of {鶏|にわとり}
- かしわ: regional term used mainly in Kansai

OTHER MEAT WORDS:
- {牛肉|ぎゅうにく} (beef)
- {豚肉|ぶたにく} (pork)
- {羊肉|ようにく} (lamb/mutton)

COMMON CUTS AND DISHES:
- {鶏|とり}むね{肉|にく}: chicken breast
- {鶏|とり}もも{肉|にく}: chicken thigh
- {焼|や}き{鳥|とり}: grilled chicken skewers
- {唐揚|からあ}げ: deep-fried chicken
- {親子丼|おやこどん}: chicken and egg rice bowl
